summary: Victor Forte worked in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Temple University by 2004 and was an assistant professor of religious studies at Albright College, attested in 2007.

Victor H. Mair was a scholar of sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Dartmouth College, SOAS, and Harvard University, later holding posts at Harvard (~1976–1979) and as professor at the University of Pennsylvania from ~1979.
Victor Henry was a linguist and Indologist. He held positions at the École Centrale de Lille (~1877–1888) and the University of Paris from 1888.

Victor Turner worked in religious studies and related fields. He studied at University College London and the University of Manchester, later chairing the Committee on Social Thought at the University of Chicago (~1968–1977).
Victoria Sujata is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Harvard University, where she studied under Michael Aris.

Vidhusekhara Bhattacharya specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University as a pandit and supervisor of collation (attested 1929–1932) and principal (attested 1944), and served as Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1943).
Vidya Dehejia is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Cambridge (~1965–1968) and held a post at Columbia University around 1982.

Vidya Niwas Mishra worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Allahabad and Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, later serving as professor of linguistics at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1968–1977).
Vilhelm Thomsen was a linguist and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Randers State School and the University of Copenhagen, where he later served as professor from ~1887 to 1913.
Vincent Arthur Smith worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1871–1900) and held a post at the University of Oxford (~1910–1920).

Vincent Breugem specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies, having studied under Lucia Dolce. He earned his MA and PhD at Leiden University, also studying at Taisho, Hanazono, and Kyoto universities, and served as a research fellow at Leiden (attested 2012).

Vincent Eltschinger works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at Collège Saint-Michel and the University of Lausanne, he held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, the University of Vienna (~2003–2015), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2015).

Vincent Goossaert works in sinology, religious studies, and history. He studied under Kristofer Schipper (~1992–1997) and held posts at the CNRS (~1998–2012), The Chinese University of Hong Kong, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2012).
Vincent Lefèvre specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the École Nationale des Chartes and Sorbonne Nouvelle University, and has served as a curator at the Musée Guimet.

Vincent Tournier specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Leiden University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, mentored by Seishi Karashima in 2008, and held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (attested 2021).
Vincenzo Vergiani specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Raffaele Torella and held a post at the University of Cambridge from ~2008.
Vindhyeshwari Prasad Dube was an Indologist who held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, attested in 1920 and 1939.

Virendra Nath Misra specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1958–1961) and later served as director of the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1990–2000).
Vishwa Nath Pathak was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts, including professor, at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, attested in 1978 and 1987.

Vishwanath Prasad Varma studied philosophy and Indology. He was taught by Dhirendra Mohan Datta, Ganga Nath Bhattacharya, and Joachim Wach, and completed doctoral supervision under Kalikinkar Datta (~1948–1950).
